observed.semantic_counterexample: Fixed circular convolution is shift equivariant. F(x)_i = i*x_i modulo p is not; F(shift e0) != shift F(e0). Thus fixed circular convolution alone cannot implement every position-sensitive mapping.

interpretation: With exact algebra and strong sparse-aware conventional baseline, Python NTT is about 12-24x faster for larger dense periodic convolution at n=512/1024 on both host OS, but materially slower for comparably sized sparse inputs, so the original general speed screen is NO_GO. A fixed convolution cannot express arbitrary position-conditioned maps by shift equivariance, but this does not rule out learned, contextual, non-convolutional or multi-component spectral architectures. No natural language or pretrained model was evaluated. Existing AC06 mod17 algebra smoke was not misreported as a new realistic model test.
next: Do not retest pure algebra; any U28 model-specific proposal needs an independently defined learned semantic architecture, original pretrained-model baseline, held-out unfamiliar text evaluation, full CPU/GPU/memory/energy accounting and separate authorization.
